text:
nina: Quick follow-up on the handoff surface between Loader and Warmup. We keep hitting an atomicity gap when a shard is being replaced during warmup + eviction.
raj: Can you sketch the failure mode again? I remember safetensors manifestless blobs made this messy.
nina: Sure — sequence: 1) Loader maps old shards, 2) Warmup starts fetching new shard in background, 3) eviction frees memory and a request races in, Loader points to new blob before warmup finishes -> partial weights on disk, crash or bad weights served.
amy: Got it. One option is to require a manifest+index for every upload so we can do index-first activation. That avoids partial-read semantics.
jeff: That's a big constraint for S3 uploaders and some HF-style bundles. We should have a compatibility path.
sato: What about an ephemeral 2-phase commit: upload blob -> upload manifest with epoch token -> manifest publish step that flips an activation pointer. Warmup only switches on manifest publish with matching epoch.
raj: That aligns with lease-based activation. Need a cheap pin to avoid eviction between manifest publish and activation.
amy: We could do: publish manifest (immutable) -> warmup obtains "activation lease" from WarmupCoordinator (short TTL) -> Loader swaps pointer only if lease present. If warmup fails lease expires and we roll back.
jeff: That still leaves a window where Loader might switch to the new manifest but warmup hasn't fully materialized local pages. We need a guarantee that Loader won't hand out GPU pointers until KV caches are primed.
nina: Right. Proposal: extend the Loader API with two ops: PREPARE_ACTIVATE(manifest, epoch) which reserves pages and returns a token; and ACTIVATE(token) which atomically swaps pointers. Warmup calls PREPARE_ACTIVATE, writes pages, then ACTIVATE.
sato: PREPARE_ACTIVATE could return a pre-allocated ephemeral mapping + reservation id. Eviction honors reservations. That should be simple on nodes with support for mmap+fadvise.
raj: How does this work for streaming shards (range requests)? PREPARE_ACTIVATE would register byte-range reservations so partial reads are allowed but not pointer swap until all ranges done.
amy: Implementation detail: warmup can request range reservations via the coordinator and get back 'range tokens'. We track completion per-token and allow ACTIVATE when all tokens ready.
jeff: We must also consider cross-node handoffs: load-balancer might route requests to old node while new node activates. We need a global registry so activation is visible cluster-wide before any non-initializing requests.
infra-bot: deploy success: warmup-coordinator v1.3.2 pushed to dev cluster :rocket: 
nina: For cluster visibility we can use a small TTL-backed registry entry in Consul/KV: set activation_state(manifest, epoch)="activating" then "active". LB checks state and denies routing to nodes in "activating" until "active".
sato: We should add metrics: reservation_count, activation_latency, failed_activations. That will help tune TTLs and eviction policies.
raj: Edgecases: aborted uploads (manifest never published) -> garbage collection. Need GC scan that checks manifests without activation for >Xh and marks blobs tombstone.
amy: Also security: manifest publish needs signing or uploader auth so no tampering with epoch tokens.
jeff: Agree. Action items:
- nina/jeff: draft PREPARE_ACTIVATE/ACTIVATE API + error semantics
- sato/amy: prototype range-reservation implementation on dev nodes
- raj: design GC + lease TTL heuristics
- infra: add cluster registry + LB check
nina: I'll start a short RFC with the API sketch and a small sequence diagram. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jeff: lgtm, nice path forward.
amy: +1
sato: thanks!
